channel.description: Recent content in Mobile_app on Best of AI

item.title: CommCare
item.description:
Program teams design forms and workflows without coding. Workers collect data offline on a phone and sync when connected. Supervisors see dashboards, and case management supports reminders for visits.

A free plan is available for small projects, and paid plans add more users and features.

KoBoToolbox and ODK are open-source options for data collection. CommCare suits community health workers and the programs that manage them.

item.title: Dragonframe
item.description:
Animators see live view, onion skinning, and timing exposure sheets while shooting. It controls DSLR cameras and DMX lighting and supports motion control rigs for camera moves. Captured frames can be reviewed and exported as video.

It runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux and is sold as a license. Independent animators and schools often use it.

Stop Motion Studio is a simpler, lower-cost option. Dragonframe suits animators who need precise capture and timing.

item.title: Mindbody
item.description:
Studios set up classes, accept bookings, and manage memberships. Clients book through a branded app or the Mindbody marketplace. Reporting and marketing tools support growth, and AI features help with messaging.

It is a subscription product with tiered pricing.

Vagaro and Zen Planner are alternatives. Mindbody suits yoga instructors who run a studio.

item.title: Pro Tools
item.description:
It handles multitrack recording, comping, and large session management. Surround and Dolby Atmos mixing are supported. It works with Avid and third-party interfaces and plug-ins, and has added assisted features such as stem separation.

It is sold by subscription or perpetual license, with a free entry version.

Logic Pro and Reaper are alternatives. Pro Tools suits sound engineers in professional studios.

item.title: Sensor Tower
item.description:
App publishers use it to benchmark competitors, find keywords, and study how top apps present themselves. App store optimization features show how listings rank for search terms. Reports cover categories, regions, and trends.

Figures are estimates, not official numbers, so they are best used for relative comparison. Pricing is custom and aimed at businesses.

AppTweak and AppFollow are alternatives. Sensor Tower suits app marketers and product teams.

item.title: UrbanFootprint
item.description:
Planners test how zoning changes or new development affect housing, jobs, and transportation. Built-in datasets cover parcels, demographics, and mobility. Results can be shared as maps and reports.

It targets professional planning teams and uses custom pricing.

ArcGIS and Carto offer related capabilities. UrbanFootprint suits city planners.

item.title: Zen Planner
item.description:
Owners set up class schedules and membership plans, and members check in with an app or kiosk. Automated billing reduces missed payments. Reports show attendance and retention.

It is a subscription product.

Mindbody and Kicksite are alternatives. Zen Planner suits martial arts instructors who run a school.

item.title: Autodesk Maya
item.description: Maya is among the oldest and most established 3D tools in entertainment. Artists use it to model characters and environments, rig them with skeletons and controls, animate them, simulate cloth, hair, fluids, and effects, and render the result. Its animation tools, including a powerful graph editor and rigging system, are the reason it became the default in animation studios. Plug-ins and scripting in Python and MEL let studios customize it to their pipelines.

item.title: Buildium
item.description:
Buildium is designed for landlords and property managers who run a few dozen to a few thousand units. A manager can list vacancies, screen applicants, sign leases online, collect rent through a resident portal, and track maintenance requests with vendors. Owners can receive statements and reports, and community associations have their own tools.

Accounting is built in, with trust accounting, bank reconciliation, and tax reports that property managers need. Mobile apps let staff handle requests in the field. Some AI features help with tasks such as drafting messages and summarizing information, and integrations connect with listing sites, screening services, and other software.

item.title: Cartoon Animator
item.description:
Cartoon Animator is built to make 2D animation approachable. You can bring in artwork, a photo, or one of the included characters, add a bone rig, and animate the character. Face tracking from a webcam drives expressions, motion templates provide walks and gestures, and audio can generate lip movement automatically.

The software includes tools for composing scenes, with backgrounds, props, and cameras, and it can export videos, image sequences, and assets for editors. It also links to Reallusion’s other products. Users can bring in layered files from Photoshop and Clip Studio, which helps artists who draw their own characters.

item.title: Firebase
item.description:
Firebase lets developers build apps without running their own servers. Its core services are Cloud Firestore and Realtime Database for storing and syncing data, Authentication for sign-in with email, phone, or social accounts, Cloud Storage for files, Hosting for websites, and Cloud Functions for server-side code. Analytics, Crashlytics, and Cloud Messaging for push notifications round out the app lifecycle tools, and SDKs support iOS, Android, web, Flutter, and Unity.

AI has become part of the platform. Gemini in Firebase helps developers write code, debug, and understand their projects, and Firebase AI Logic gives apps a secure way to call Gemini and other models directly from the client. Genkit is an open-source framework for building AI features and agents, and Firebase Studio provides a browser-based environment for prototyping apps with AI assistance.

item.title: Housecall Pro
item.description:
Housecall Pro helps small service companies run their operations. Office staff schedule jobs and dispatch technicians on a calendar and map, customers receive confirmations and arrival notifications, and technicians use a mobile app to see their jobs, send estimates, collect signatures, and take payments on site. Invoices and payments flow into accounting.

The platform includes marketing and sales tools. Review requests, email campaigns, and a customer database help a business grow repeat work, and a booking widget lets homeowners schedule online. Some AI features answer calls and messages, help with scheduling and follow-ups, and summarize job details so owners can stay on top of the business.

item.title: LiveKit
item.description:
LiveKit started as an open-source WebRTC platform that handles the hard parts of real-time communication: routing audio and video between many participants, scaling to large rooms, and working across web and mobile. Developers use its SDKs to build video conferencing, livestreaming, telehealth, and interactive broadcast features, and can run it on their own servers or use the hosted LiveKit Cloud.

The company became prominent in voice AI. The Agents framework lets developers build agents that listen, think with a language model, and speak back, with low latency, handling details such as turn-taking and interruptions. It supports telephony so agents can answer phone calls, plus plugins for speech recognition, language, and voice providers. LiveKit powers voice features in well-known AI products, which helped establish it as a standard for real-time AI.

item.title: Mighty Networks
item.description:
Mighty Networks is a platform for building a membership community. A creator sets up a space with feeds, groups, live events, and online courses, and members join by paying a subscription or one-time fee. The pitch is an experience that feels like your own app, with mobile apps that can carry your brand.

Monetization is built in. Creators can charge for memberships, courses, and events, offer tiered access, and run bundles. The AI assistant helps with tasks such as naming a community, drafting posts and course outlines, and suggesting engagement ideas. Analytics show member activity, which helps community managers improve retention.

item.title: Speak
item.description:
Speak puts spoken practice first. Instead of tapping through vocabulary drills, you speak aloud in lessons that simulate real situations such as ordering food, introducing yourself, or having a job interview. The app listens, corrects pronunciation and grammar, and prompts you to try again, so you gain confidence speaking, which many apps neglect.

An AI tutor handles open-ended conversation. You can discuss topics you choose, practice roleplays, and ask the tutor to explain mistakes, with the system adapting to your level. The app began with a focus on English for Korean speakers and has expanded to teach other languages, with courses designed for particular native languages. It was developed with backing from OpenAI’s startup fund.

item.title: Thunkable
item.description:
Thunkable lets people build mobile apps without writing code. The designer places buttons, lists, maps, and other components on a screen, and a visual blocks editor, similar to Scratch, defines the logic. A live test app on your phone shows changes as you make them, which makes learning fast.

Apps are native, not just web wrappers, and can use device features like the camera, location, and notifications. Connections to databases, APIs, and services like Firebase and Airtable allow real functionality. Schools use Thunkable to teach app creation, and small businesses and entrepreneurs use it to build prototypes and simple tools.

item.title: Taromi
item.description:
Taromi pairs the practice of tarot with AI interpretation. A user poses a question, draws cards from a virtual deck, and receives a written reading that explains the cards in context. Many users treat it as a prompt for reflection more than a prediction.

The format is easy to use daily, with options for different spreads and for saving past readings. Like horoscopes, tarot has no proven ability to foretell events, and readings generated by AI are creative text, not guidance backed by evidence.

item.title: Esko
item.description:
Esko serves the packaging and label industries. Designers use ArtiosCAD to create the structural design of boxes and cartons, with dielines that show cuts and folds. ArtPro+ and related tools prepare artwork for printing, handling color, trapping, and layout across the many steps between a design and the press.

Workflow tools automate preparation and approval. Software checks files for errors, compares versions, and routes proofs, which reduces mistakes in printed packaging where a typo can mean a costly reprint. Cloud platforms support collaboration between brands, designers, and printers, and AI helps with checking and automating routine tasks.

item.title: Nutrium
item.description:
Nutrium helps nutrition professionals run a practice. They manage clients, schedule appointments, and keep records of measurements and goals, while clients use an app to log meals and see their plan. A food database with nutrient data supports analysis and meal planning.

AI speeds up plan creation by proposing menus that fit a client’s calorie and nutrient targets and preferences, which the dietitian then adjusts. Reports and communication tools keep clients engaged between visits.

item.title: Vagaro
item.description:
Vagaro runs the front desk for beauty and wellness businesses. Clients book online or through a marketplace app, staff manage calendars, take payments, and track inventory. Reminders and no-show protection reduce lost appointments.

Marketing tools include email and text campaigns, loyalty programs, and a presence on the Vagaro marketplace. AI answers calls and messages, helps book appointments, and suggests promotions.

Vagaro charges a monthly fee per business, with add-ons and payment processing fees. Alternatives include Fresha, Booksy, StyleSeat, Square Appointments, and Mindbody. Vagaro suits salons, spas, and studios.

item.title: ChatGPT Atlas
item.description:
Atlas puts ChatGPT inside the browser. A sidebar assistant can see the page you are on, so you can ask it to summarize an article, explain a table, compare products across tabs, or draft a reply in context. The address bar can also act as a chat prompt, and the browser can remember context from your browsing if you turn that on.

Agent mode goes further. The assistant can take actions on your behalf, such as navigating to a site, filling in a form, or doing research across several pages, while you watch and can take over. This capability is powerful and also risky, since web pages can contain instructions meant to trick an agent, a problem known as prompt injection.

item.title: Comet
item.description:
Comet makes the assistant part of the browser. Instead of copying content into a chatbot, users can ask questions about the page they are on, compare information across tabs, summarize a thread, or have the assistant search and collect results. Perplexity’s answer engine is the default way to search.

An agent mode lets the assistant take actions, such as filling in forms, managing a calendar or inbox, or completing a purchase flow, while the user watches and can step in. This gives it the power and the risks of any browsing agent, including exposure to prompt injection from malicious web pages.

item.title: Born to Found
item.description:
Born to Found guides first-time founders through the early journey. It divides company building into stages, such as validating an idea, building a first product, and finding customers, and supplies playbooks and checklists for each, so a founder knows what to focus on at their point.

An AI coach answers questions and reviews work, drawing on the founder’s stage and project details. This offers a low-cost alternative to mentors for people who lack access to experienced advisors, and a structure to keep going when the path is unclear.

item.title: Hour One
item.description:
Hour One produces videos with AI avatars. A user chooses a virtual presenter, pastes a script, and the platform generates a video of the presenter speaking, with options for language, voice, and background. Custom avatars can be created from real people with their consent.

It is aimed at companies that need to make many videos, such as training modules and product updates, without arranging film shoots each time. Changing a script and regenerating the video is faster than reshooting, and translations extend the same video to new languages.

item.title: Moonvalley
item.description:
Moonvalley builds generative video for creative professionals. Its Marey model is trained on licensed and rights-cleared footage, which the company positions as a safer choice for studios concerned about copyright. Users generate clips and have controls over camera movement, motion, and style.

Filmmakers use it to visualize scenes, build storyboards, and test ideas before expensive shoots, and agencies use it for concept work. The company works with filmmakers and studios, aiming at professional workflows more than casual social content.

item.title: 8th Wall
item.description:
8th Wall made AR available through a link. Developers built experiences using web technologies, and users opened them in a phone browser by scanning a QR code or tapping a link, with no app download. Brands used it for marketing campaigns, product try-ons, games, and events, and agencies liked that it worked across iOS and Android. Features included world tracking, image targets, face effects, and, later, location-based AR.

Niantic, the company behind Pokémon Go, acquired 8th Wall, and its technology was used alongside Niantic’s mapping and spatial work. Niantic Spatial, the spinoff focused on geospatial AI, then ended access to the 8th Wall platform. Hosted projects were given time to keep running, and the engine was released as open source, so developers can still use its code.

item.title: Bizzabo
item.description: Bizzabo is a software platform for corporate and large-scale event teams. Planners build event websites, sell tickets and handle registration, manage speakers and agendas, and track who attends. On site, it supports badge printing and check-in, and a mobile app lets attendees see the schedule, message each other, and use polls or Q&A during sessions. For virtual and hybrid events, it can stream sessions and bring remote attendees into the same experience.

item.title: Deepdub
item.description: Deepdub works with studios, streamers, and media companies that need content in many languages. Its technology translates the dialogue and generates new speech in the target language, in a voice that matches the original performer, with timing that fits the picture. The goal is dubbing that carries over emotion and character, not the flat voice of a basic text-to-speech engine. It supports over a hundred languages and uses licensed voices, which matters for rights and union considerations.

item.title: Mabl
item.description: Mabl aims to make automated testing less fragile. Teams record or describe user flows, such as signing in or checking out, and the platform turns them into automated tests that run in the cloud across browsers and devices. A low-code approach means QA engineers and developers can create tests without writing everything in code, though scripting is available when needed. Tests run on a schedule or in CI/CD pipelines when code changes.

item.title: NaturalReader
item.description:
NaturalReader turns reading into listening. You paste text, upload a document or PDF, or use the Chrome extension to read a web page, and it reads aloud in a voice you choose, with adjustable speed. Highlighting of each word as it is spoken helps learners follow along, and the tool supports many languages and accents. OCR features can read text from images and scanned pages.

It serves education and accessibility needs. Students with dyslexia, ADHD, or visual impairments use it to access materials, professionals use it to review documents on the go, and teachers use it with classroom content. Premium plans offer higher-quality AI voices, more file formats, and commercial use for creating audio, while a free version covers personal use with basic voices.

item.title: PatSnap
item.description:
PatSnap serves teams that need to understand the patent landscape. Its search covers a very large collection of patents and scientific literature worldwide, and semantic search finds relevant documents from a description of an invention instead of exact keywords. Users can analyze who is filing in a technology area, map clusters of related patents, track competitors, and check whether an idea has been patented before.

Several products fit different jobs. Tools help with prior art searches before filing, freedom-to-operate checks before launching a product, and landscape analysis to guide R&D strategy. AI assistants summarize patents, extract key claims, and answer questions about a technology, and workflows let teams share results and collaborate. The platform also covers non-patent literature and market information for innovation scouting.

item.title: Sentry
item.description:
Sentry tells developers when their code breaks and why. By adding an SDK to an app, errors are reported with stack traces, the environment, the user’s actions leading up to the problem, and the release that introduced it. Sentry groups duplicate errors into single issues, sends alerts, and links to the relevant commit, so teams can fix a bug quickly rather than discovering it from user complaints.

Beyond error tracking, Sentry monitors performance with tracing that shows slow requests and database queries, and session replay records what the user saw. Cron monitoring watches scheduled jobs, and release health tracks crash-free sessions. Its AI assistant, Seer, analyzes issues to suggest root causes and can propose fixes, and tools for monitoring AI applications trace model calls. It supports most languages and frameworks, and integrates with GitHub, Slack, and Jira.

item.title: TestFit
item.description:
TestFit speeds up the feasibility stage of real estate development. A user draws a site boundary and sets rules such as unit mix, parking ratios, setbacks, and building types, and TestFit generates layouts that fit, updating in real time as constraints change. It reports metrics like unit counts, parking, rentable area, and efficiency, which let developers judge whether a site works before investing heavily.

It handles multiple product types, including apartment buildings, townhomes, self-storage, hotels, and parking structures, and exports to common design tools such as Revit and CAD for the next stage. Cost and revenue features help assess returns, and collaboration tools let teams share scenarios. Generative algorithms explore many arrangements to find efficient solutions.

item.title: Adalo
item.description:
Adalo lets people without programming skills build mobile apps. You design screens with a drag-and-drop editor, add components such as lists, forms, and buttons, set up a database for your data, and define what happens when users interact. It handles user accounts, payments, and push notifications, and produces apps that can be published to the Apple App Store and Google Play, as well as web apps.

AI features speed up the first draft: you can describe an app and have the builder generate screens and data structures, then refine them manually. A marketplace of components and integrations extends functionality, and connections to external databases and APIs allow more complex apps. Typical projects include community directories, booking apps, marketplaces, internal tools, and simple social apps.

item.title: Adobe Premiere Pro AI
item.description: Premiere Pro is a timeline-based video editor used for everything from YouTube videos and corporate content to broadcast and feature work. It handles most camera formats, supports proxy workflows for heavy footage, and connects directly to After Effects, Audition, and other Adobe apps. That connection is a large part of why editing teams keep using it: a project can pass between an editor, a colorist, and a motion designer without leaving the Adobe ecosystem.

item.title: Altered AI
item.description:
Altered focuses on voice conversion, sometimes called speech-to-speech. You record a performance, and the system re-voices it in another voice from its library while keeping the timing, emotion, and delivery of the original. That differs from text-to-speech, where the machine invents the performance. For productions, it means one actor can voice several characters, or a performance can be changed to match a different character without a second recording session.

The tools are designed for professionals. Altered Studio provides a way to process recordings and fine-tune results, and the platform includes text-to-speech and voice cloning options for productions that need them. Typical customers are game studios, audiobook makers, animation and film teams, and agencies that localize content. Licensed voices matter in this field, since using someone’s voice without permission raises legal and ethical issues.

item.title: Apple Maps
item.description: Apple Maps comes installed on every Apple device and has improved a great deal since its rocky start. It provides turn-by-turn driving directions, walking, cycling, and public transit routes, plus lane guidance and speed limit information. Features such as Look Around give a street-level view of many cities, detailed maps show buildings and landmarks in 3D, and downloadable offline maps work without a connection. Guides collect recommended places in a city, and you can share your arrival time with friends.

item.title: Arc Browser
item.description: Arc reimagined the browser. Instead of a row of tabs across the top, it uses a vertical sidebar where tabs are grouped into spaces, such as work and personal, each with its own pinned items and theme. Tabs that you do not use are archived automatically, and features like split view, boosts for customizing websites, and easels for collecting ideas made it a favorite of power users and designers. It is built on Chromium, so most Chrome extensions work.

item.title: Avoma
item.description: Avoma joins sales, customer success, and recruiting meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then records and transcribes them and produces notes organized by meeting type. Instead of a generic summary, it uses templates suited to the call, such as a discovery call or a customer check-in, and pulls out action items, objections, and next steps. Notes and key fields can be pushed into CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, which saves reps from doing data entry after every call.

item.title: Craft Docs
item.description: Craft aims to make notes and documents that look good. It works as a block-based editor where text, images, tables, and cards live in nested pages that you can reorganize easily. Native apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch are fast and polished, with offline support, and there is also a web and Windows version. Daily notes and tasks cover personal organization, and Spaces and collections keep larger projects tidy.

item.title: Dark Sky
item.description:
Dark Sky changed expectations for weather apps. Using radar data and machine learning, it predicted when rain or snow would start and stop at your exact location, with messages such as light rain starting in 10 minutes. That focus on the next hour, rather than a general daily forecast, made it popular with people who walk, run, or commute, and its design was clean and quick to read.

It also offered an API that thousands of apps and websites used for weather data. Developers valued its simple interface and detailed forecasts, which made it a common building block in other products. Apple acquired the company, integrated its technology into Apple Weather, and then retired the Dark Sky app and its API.

item.title: Dimensions
item.description:
Dimensions connects different kinds of research outputs. Instead of searching only for papers, users can see how a grant led to publications, which patents cite a study, and whether a trial or policy document refers to it. The linked structure helps trace the path from funding to impact.

Institutions, funders, and researchers use it for several purposes. Universities benchmark their output, funders track results of the grants they award, and companies look for experts and emerging fields. AI features summarize results, help with literature searches, and surface connections, and APIs let organizations pull data into their own systems.

item.title: Dynamic Yield
item.description:
Dynamic Yield helps businesses show each customer the content most likely to interest them. It collects behavior data from web, mobile, and email channels, builds profiles and segments, and uses machine learning to choose which products, banners, or messages to show. Retailers use it for recommendations like customers also bought, personalized homepages, and tailored promotions.

The platform also covers testing and optimization. Teams run experiments to compare versions of pages, with statistics to determine winners, and use triggers such as exit intent to present timely offers. Integrations connect with e-commerce platforms, customer data platforms, and marketing tools, and AI features suggest audiences and automate decisions. It supports use in industries including retail, travel, banking, and media.

item.title: Elai.io
item.description:
Elai.io is aimed at people who need a presenter video without filming. A user picks from a library of avatars, enters a script or imports a document, selects a voice and language, and the platform produces a video of the avatar speaking. Backgrounds, text, and media can be added in a slide-like editor.

Typical uses are training videos, product explainers, and marketing content, and the ability to translate into many languages helps localize quickly. Custom avatars can be created from a person’s footage. Features such as converting articles or links into videos speed up content creation.

item.title: ElevenLabs
item.description:
ElevenLabs is known for natural-sounding synthetic speech. Users type text and choose a voice, or clone a voice from a sample, and get audio that carries intonation and emotion. The platform supports dozens of languages and accents and offers a library of voices.

Its products now span several uses. Dubbing translates video into other languages while keeping the speaker’s voice, audiobook and narration tools produce long-form audio, and a conversational agent platform builds voice assistants that talk with customers in real time. Music and sound effect generation, plus speech to text, round out the suite. An API lets developers embed these features.

item.title: ElevenLabs
item.description: ElevenLabs is best known for text-to-speech that sounds like a person rather than a robot. You paste in a script, choose a voice from a large library or make your own, and the tool reads it with natural pacing and emotion. The same voice can speak dozens of languages, which makes it a popular option for audiobooks, YouTube narration, e-learning, game characters, and accessibility. Voice cloning builds a copy of a voice from a recording, and there are safeguards around it: you are meant to have the speaker’s permission, and some features require identity checks.

item.title: FlutterFlow
item.description: FlutterFlow combines the speed of a visual builder with real code. You design screens by dragging widgets, define logic with a visual action editor, and connect to backends such as Firebase, Supabase, or any API. Because it generates Flutter code, apps run natively on iOS and Android and also on the web, and you can export the code to continue development in a standard IDE, which avoids the lock-in of many no-code tools.

item.title: Gemini
item.description: Gemini is Google’s family of AI models and the assistant built on top of them. You can use it in the standalone Gemini app and website, but it also shows up inside the products many people already use: it can help draft emails in Gmail, rewrite text in Docs, summarize files in Drive, and answer questions on Android phones. If most of your work and personal life already runs on a Google account, that integration is the main reason to choose Gemini over another assistant.

item.title: Gen-2
item.description:
Runway builds generative video tools for filmmakers, designers, and creators. Gen-3 Alpha was a major step in its line, generating short clips from a text prompt or an image with better detail, motion, and consistency than earlier versions. It supported controls for camera movement and style.

Runway’s platform around its models includes editing tools, motion brush features, and ways to extend or modify clips. Its research focuses on world models and video generation for creative work, and the company works with studios and artists. The newer models in the line have largely taken the place of Gen-3.

item.title: Google Assistant
item.description: Google Assistant is the voice assistant that ships on Android phones, Nest speakers and displays, Android Auto, Wear OS watches, and many third-party smart home devices. You wake it with a phrase or a button, then ask it to set a timer, add a calendar event, send a message, play music, or turn off the lights. It works well for short, concrete commands, and a large ecosystem of smart home brands supports it, which made it one of the more capable options for controlling a connected home.

item.title: Google Translate
item.description: Google Translate is the translation tool most people try first. You type or paste text and get a translation in a second, with the language detected automatically. The mobile app adds the features travelers rely on: a camera mode that replaces text on signs and menus, a conversation mode that translates both sides of a spoken exchange, handwriting input, and offline language packs that work without a connection. Chrome can translate whole web pages, and you can upload documents and get a translated copy.

item.title: Helpshift
item.description:
Helpshift places support inside the app. Users reach help from a screen in a game or mobile product, without leaving to email, and conversations carry context about the device, account, and recent activity. Agents see this information and respond in the same thread.

AI reduces the load. Intent detection reads messages, classifies the issue, and routes it to the right team, while chatbots answer common questions and collect details before a human steps in. A knowledge base and automation tools support self-service, and analytics track satisfaction and resolution times.

item.title: Inworld AI
item.description:
Inworld AI began by giving non-player characters in games personality, memory, and the ability to converse. Developers define a character’s background, goals, and knowledge, and the platform handles dialogue, emotion, and behavior using language models, so players can talk to characters freely instead of choosing from scripted options. Integrations with Unity and Unreal Engine make it easy to add to games.

The company has evolved toward infrastructure for real-time AI applications. Its runtime helps developers build and scale voice and conversational experiences with low latency, and it offers text-to-speech models and tools for combining speech recognition, language models, and voice into agents. Use cases extend from games to training simulations, companions, and consumer apps with talking characters.

item.title: iZotope RX
item.description:
RX is the tool engineers reach for when audio is flawed. Its spectral display shows sound as an image, making it possible to see and remove specific problems, such as a cough, a phone buzz, or a chair squeak, without affecting the rest. Modules cover denoising, de-clicking, de-hum, de-reverb, de-clipping, and other repair tasks, and are used by post-production teams, podcast producers, forensic analysts, and musicians.

Machine learning powers its newer tools. Dialogue Isolate separates speech from background sounds, Music Rebalance lets you adjust the levels of vocals, bass, and drums in a finished mix, and Spectral Recovery restores high frequencies lost in low-quality files. Dialogue Contour and other features help produce consistent speech. It works as a standalone editor and as plugins in digital audio workstations and video editors.

item.title: Kaedim
item.description:
Kaedim addresses a slow stage in game and digital content production: turning concept art into 3D assets. You upload an image of a character, prop, or environment piece, and Kaedim produces a 3D model that matches it. The aim is to give artists a solid starting point they can refine, which cuts down the days of modeling work needed for each asset.

The service has been known for mixing machine learning with human review. Models go through checks by 3D artists who clean up errors before they are delivered, which improves reliability compared with fully automatic generators, but may slow turnaround. Output can be downloaded in common formats and used in engines like Unity and Unreal or imported into Blender and Maya for editing. Teams use it for game props, virtual production, and prototyping product ideas.

item.title: Lensa AI
item.description:
Lensa is a mobile photo editor best known for a single viral feature. Magic Avatars let users upload a set of selfies and receive a collection of stylized portraits in the style of fantasy art, anime, or illustration. The effect spread quickly on social media, driving downloads and making many people aware of AI image generation. The avatars are created with a model fine-tuned on each user’s photos.

The core of the app is a selfie and portrait editor. It offers retouching for skin and eyes, background replacement, blur and sharpening, and a range of filters and effects. Subscribers get access to the full tool set, and Magic Avatars can be purchased as packs. Prisma Labs, the developer, also makes other photo and AI apps.

item.title: Llamasoft
item.description:
Llamasoft helped companies answer strategic supply chain questions. Where should factories and warehouses be placed? How would costs change if a port closes or demand shifts? Its software builds a digital model of a supply network, then uses optimization and simulation to test alternatives and recommend the best configuration, balancing cost, service levels, and risk. Large manufacturers, retailers, and consumer goods companies used it for network design and planning.

Coupa acquired Llamasoft and folded it into its business spend management platform, so customers can connect supply chain decisions with procurement and spend data. The technology continues under Coupa branding, with capabilities such as network optimization, inventory and sourcing analysis, and demand sensing, supported by machine learning and a digital twin of the supply chain.

item.title: Ludo.ai
item.description:
Ludo.ai aims to speed up the early stages of game development. Designers can brainstorm game concepts and mechanics, get suggestions based on trends in app stores, and generate descriptions and feature lists. A market research tool analyzes top-performing games to show what genres and themes are popular, which helps indie studios and publishers decide what to build.

The platform includes asset generation. It can produce concept art and character designs, sprites and sprite sheets, short animations, UI elements, and sound effects and music from prompts, and convert images into basic 3D models in some plans. Outputs are intended for prototypes and mockups to test ideas quickly, and can be exported for use in engines like Unity.

item.title: Luma AI
item.description:
Luma began in 3D. Its first app let anyone capture an object or space with a phone camera and turn it into a photorealistic 3D scene using neural radiance fields and, later, Gaussian splatting. People used it to scan products, rooms, and sculptures, and share them in a browser or export them to 3D tools. It also released Genie, a text-to-3D model that creates 3D assets from a description.

The company has since shifted its attention to video and multimodal generation. Its Ray video models create clips from text or images, and tools for editing existing footage, keyframes, and reframing give creators control. These models are available through the Dream Machine app and an API. Luma has also introduced agents that plan and carry out creative work across text, images, video, and audio, and it works with studios on production workflows.

item.title: Mematic
item.description:
Mematic makes meme creation quick on a phone. Users pick a template from a large library or upload their own image, add captions in the classic style, and share to social networks and messaging apps. The interface is built for thumb use, so formatting text is fast.

The app offers sticker and filter options, categories of trending templates, and tools for adding emoji and shapes. A premium subscription removes ads and watermarks and adds more templates and features.

item.title: Microsoft Translator
item.description:
Microsoft Translator covers the common translation needs. You can type or paste text, speak into a phone for conversation translation, translate images and documents, and use offline language packs when traveling. Multi-device conversation mode lets several people speak in different languages and see translations on their own screens, which suits meetings and travel.

It’s integrated throughout Microsoft products. Teams offers live captions and translated meetings, Office apps can translate documents and text, and Edge translates web pages. For developers and businesses, Azure AI Translator provides APIs for text, document, and speech translation, with custom models and glossaries, and options to run in containers.

item.title: Pi
item.description:
Pi was built to be a kind and curious conversational partner instead of a productivity tool. Its responses are short, warm, and conversational, and it often asks follow-up questions, which made it a favorite with people who wanted to talk through ideas, plans, or feelings in a low-pressure setting. It supports voice conversations with several voices, which suits casual use.

Inflection AI, founded by former DeepMind and LinkedIn leaders, launched Pi with the aim of making a personal AI. The company later saw its founders and much of its team join Microsoft, and it pivoted to licensing its models to enterprises. Pi remains online as a free consumer product at pi.ai and in apps, but active development has slowed, and the messaging integrations it once had are gone.

item.title: Pixelcut
item.description:
Pixelcut focuses on product images. A seller photographs an item, removes the background in one tap, and places the product on a clean or styled backdrop. AI can generate scenes that suit a product, add shadows, and upscale low-resolution pictures.

Batch tools process many images, and templates help create ads, social posts, and listing graphics. The mobile app is popular with small sellers who shoot products with a phone.

Pixelcut has a free tier and paid plans. AI-generated scenes should still show the product accurately to avoid returns. Alternatives include Photoroom, Canva, Pebblely, Remove.bg, and Adobe Express. Pixelcut suits small online sellers.

item.title: Promethean AI
item.description:
Promethean AI addresses the labor involved in building 3D environments. An artist describes what they want in a scene, such as a cluttered study or a forest clearing, and the assistant selects assets from a library, places them with sensible arrangement and variation, and assembles a draft environment. The aim is to automate repetitive dressing and layout so artists can focus on art direction.

The tool learns from the studio’s own assets and preferences, so output stays consistent with the project’s look, and it integrates with common creative software and engines. It was aimed at game studios, film and virtual production teams, and architectural visualization, where large environments must be filled with believable detail.

item.title: Replica Studios
item.description:
Replica Studios was an Australian startup that made AI voices aimed at creative productions. Its library offered voices of professional actors who had agreed to license their performances, and its tools let game developers and filmmakers generate dialogue with emotion and style. Integrations for game engines such as Unreal and Unity made it easy to put placeholder or final voices into a project, and it also supported voice conversion.

The company drew attention for working with actors instead of against them. It signed an agreement with the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA on terms for licensing digital voice replicas in games, which some actors welcomed and others criticized as inadequate. That debate was part of a wider fight over how AI voices should be used in entertainment, which continues.

item.title: Resemble AI
item.description: Resemble AI builds voices for products and productions. You provide recordings of a speaker, with consent, and the platform trains a voice model that can read any text in that voice, or convert one person’s speech into another voice in real time. Companies use it for branded voices, localization, games, call centers, and media. An API makes it possible to generate speech in applications, and the system supports multiple languages and emotional control.

item.title: Rive
item.description: Rive aims to make animation behave like part of an app. In its editor, designers draw vector shapes, rig them with bones, and animate them on a timeline. The key difference from video or GIF is the state machine: animations can have states and transitions that react to inputs, such as a button being pressed, a character getting closer, or a progress value changing. This lets one asset handle many behaviors.

item.title: Scenario
item.description:
Scenario is built around consistency, which is the main challenge of using generative AI in game production. A studio uploads examples of its art, and Scenario trains a custom model that learns the style, so the characters, props, and environments it generates look like they belong in the same game. Artists can use it to create concepts, variations, and finished assets faster.

The platform covers more than still images. It can generate sprites, textures, icons, and UI elements, create variations of existing pieces, convert images into 3D models, and offers workflows for upscaling and cleaning outputs. An API and plugins connect it to game engines and pipelines, and team features support collaboration and asset management. The focus is on production use by studios and indie developers.

item.title: Siri
item.description: Siri is the assistant that comes with every Apple device. You say “Hey Siri” or hold a button, then ask it to send a message, set a timer, call someone, play music, adjust a setting, or control HomeKit devices. It works across Apple’s hardware, so the same assistant is on your wrist, in your car through CarPlay, and on a smart speaker. Its biggest advantage is how deeply it ties into the system, since it can act on messages, calendars, reminders, and photos without extra setup.

item.title: SketchUp
item.description: SketchUp is known for being easy to learn. Its core idea is pushing and pulling flat shapes into 3D forms, which makes it quick to sketch a building, a room, or a piece of furniture. Architects use it for early design, interior designers for layouts, and construction and woodworking professionals for planning and shop drawings. The 3D Warehouse offers a huge library of free models of furniture, fixtures, and building components.

item.title: Spark Mail
item.description:
Spark is an email client that works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, and other accounts. Its Smart Inbox sorts messages into categories, putting people and important mail first and keeping newsletters and notifications out of the way. Features such as snooze, send later, follow-up reminders, and quick replies make it faster to process mail, and a unified inbox combines accounts.

Collaboration is a differentiator. Teams can share emails, comment privately on messages, and draft replies together before sending, which suits small teams who handle shared mailboxes. AI features in the paid tier help write and rewrite emails, summarize long threads, and suggest replies, and a feature can search by asking questions. The app is available on Apple devices, Android, and Windows.

item.title: StarryAI
item.description:
StarryAI brought AI art generation to phones. In the app, you enter a text prompt, pick an art style or model, and receive images within a minute or so. Styles range from fantasy and anime to realism and abstract, and you can use an image as a starting point for variations. It’s aimed at hobbyists and creators who want art for wallpapers, profile pictures, book covers, or game concepts.

Features support experimentation. You can control aspect ratio, choose among models, and upscale results, and a gallery shows creations from other users for inspiration. Different pricing tiers offer more credits and faster generation, and the terms for commercial use vary by plan, with ownership of outputs depending on the subscription.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia produces videos with digital presenters. Users select from a library of avatars or create a custom one, paste a script, choose a voice and language, and receive a finished video. The editor handles slides, text, and media.

Companies use it for training, onboarding, product explainers, and communications, often replacing costly shoots. Translations let one video serve many markets. Recent features add interactive videos, screen recording, and avatars with more expressive delivery.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia lets companies produce videos without cameras, studios, or actors. A user writes or pastes a script, selects an AI avatar from a library of presenters or creates a custom one, and the platform generates a video with natural speech and lip movement. Scenes, slides, screen recordings, and media can be combined, and editing the script and regenerating takes the place of a reshoot.

The platform is built for business use. It supports a large number of languages, so one video can be localized quickly, and offers templates, brand kits, and collaboration features. Interactive and agent-style avatars can respond to viewers, and an API lets teams automate video creation. Enterprise features cover security, compliance, and consent controls, since custom avatars require permission from the person depicted. Companies commonly use it for learning and development, onboarding, product explainers, and sales content.

item.title: Topaz Photo AI
item.description:
Topaz Photo AI aims to fix the technical flaws in photos with little effort. When you open an image, it analyzes the content and suggests corrections, using models for noise reduction, sharpening, and increasing resolution. It handles problems like grainy high-ISO shots, soft focus, and motion blur, and can enlarge photos while adding believable detail. Many wildlife, sports, and event photographers use it to rescue difficult images.

The tool also offers face recovery, light adjustment, color balance, and a way to apply different adjustments to selected subjects. It can be run as a standalone application, as an external editor from Lightroom, or as a plugin for Photoshop, and processes batches of images. Models run locally on your computer and benefit from a good graphics card.

item.title: UiPath
item.description:
UiPath popularized robotic process automation, in which software robots mimic what a person does on a screen. Developers build automations in a studio by recording and arranging steps such as clicking, copying data between systems, and filling forms, and run them on servers or desktops. This is valuable for companies with legacy systems that lack APIs, since bots can work through the same interfaces people use.

The platform has expanded into AI. Document understanding extracts data from invoices and forms, process mining reveals which workflows are worth automating, and agent tools let AI agents plan and carry out tasks, orchestrated alongside robots and people. The Maestro orchestration layer coordinates agents, robots, and human steps, and governance features control access and auditing.

item.title: Vyond
item.description:
Vyond focuses on business animation. Users build videos from libraries of characters, props, and backgrounds, choosing actions and expressions for each character and arranging scenes on a timeline. The style is a recognizable cartoon format popular in corporate training, compliance courses, and explainer videos, and the tool makes it possible to produce them without animation skills.

AI features reduce the work of getting started. A text-to-video capability generates a draft video from a script or prompt, including scenes, characters, and voiceover, which you can then edit. Other tools produce voices in many languages, help with translations, and match lip sync. Branded templates and shared libraries help teams keep their videos consistent, and enterprise features cover security and administration.

item.title: Fantastical
item.description:
Fantastical is known for natural language entry. A user types a phrase such as lunch with Sam next Tuesday at noon, and the app creates the event with the right time, place, and attendees. It shows calendars from many accounts in one view, including Google, iCloud, and Exchange, along with tasks and reminders.

Scheduling features help with coordination. Users can share availability and let others book time, propose several slots to a group, and attach video conference details automatically. Newer AI features help with preparation for meetings and smart suggestions, and the app integrates with other tools through its calendar sets and openings.

item.title: Respeecher
item.description:
Respeecher works through speech-to-speech conversion. A performer records a line, and the system transforms it into the voice of a target speaker, keeping the performer’s emotion and timing. This differs from text-to-speech, which generates speech from scratch and can lack nuance.

Productions have used it to recreate the voices of actors who are unavailable, age or de-age a voice, and dub into other languages while preserving a character’s sound. The company emphasizes licensing and consent from voice owners.

item.title: Unakin
item.description:
Unakin targets game studios. Its agents take requests in natural language and help create parts of a game, such as environments, items, interfaces, and gameplay logic, and assist with finding and fixing bugs. The pitch is a smaller team doing more in less time.

Prototyping is a main use, letting designers test ideas before investing heavily. Code assistance for Unity helps developers learn unfamiliar parts of a project.

Independent information is limited, so confirm current availability and pricing on the company’s site. Game development has quality and licensing concerns about AI-generated assets. Alternatives include Unity’s AI tools, Scenario, Inworld, Convai, and general coding assistants like Cursor. Unakin suits game teams exploring AI helpers.

item.title: Chai
item.description:
Chai lets people talk to a huge variety of AI personalities. Users browse or search for characters, such as a friendly companion, a fantasy hero, or a fictional figure, and chat in a messaging-style interface. Creators can build their own characters by writing a short description and a first message, and they are shared with the community, which has produced a very large catalog.

The experience is aimed at entertainment and companionship. The AI maintains a persona and some memory of the conversation, and the app offers features such as voice and image options and a feed of popular bots. Free users see ads and message limits, while subscribers get faster responses and more features.

item.title: Leonardo AI
item.description:
Leonardo.ai began as a tool for game developers who needed lots of consistent assets. Users generate images from text prompts with a choice of Leonardo’s own models and others, then refine them with inpainting, upscaling, and background removal. Fine-tuned models for characters, environments, items, and concept art made it popular with game artists, illustrators, and designers who care about a particular visual style.

Customization is a major draw. You can train your own models on a set of images to produce consistent characters or brand looks, use reference images to control composition and style, and draw on a canvas to guide generation. The platform has added video generation and animation of stills, along with an API for developers. A community feed lets users see what others are making and borrow prompts.

item.title: MarketAlerts.ai
item.description:
MarketAlerts.ai watches the market on behalf of its users. Investors list their holdings, and the service monitors news, filings, price moves, and other events, sending alerts when something relevant happens and summarizing why it might matter. Some alerts include AI-generated signals about possible actions.

Such tools save time for people who cannot follow the market all day, but they carry risks. AI-generated trade signals are not reliable predictions, markets are unpredictable, and acting on automated signals can lose money. Nothing here is financial advice.

item.title: Mumble AI
item.description:
Mumble AI is built around talking instead of typing. Users dictate ideas or record meetings, and the app turns speech into structured notes, highlighting tasks and decisions. Apps on Mac and iPhone sync so a thought captured on the go is waiting at the desk.

It targets busy professionals who think out loud: managers between meetings, founders, and consultants. Features include summaries, task extraction, and searchable archives.

Independent information about Mumble AI is limited, so check where audio is processed and stored. It has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Otter, Granola, Superwhisper, Voicenotes, and Apple Notes with transcription. Mumble AI suits people who prefer to capture notes by voice.

item.title: Tripo3D
item.description:
Tripo focuses on speed and consistency. Enter a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D model in seconds to a minute, with options for style and level of detail. The models are meant to be usable in games, animation, 3D printing, and e-commerce, and the platform provides downloads in common formats like GLB, FBX, and OBJ.

Features go beyond the initial generation. Tools can create cleaner topology for animation, generate or replace textures from a prompt, add skeletons so characters can be posed, and apply animations. A segmentation option separates a model into parts for editing. An API and integrations with Blender, Unity, Unreal, and other applications fit it into creative pipelines, and a community library offers starting points.
